summary: Discovery focused on dedicated reserved GPUs with isolation requirements for PHI workloads. Customer wants a mixed model: base reserved capacity for steady inference, isolated tenancy per environment, and controlled burst to a shared pool. Key concerns: deterministic latency SLOs, data residency, KMS/HSM integration, and cost predictability. Agreed to run a benchmark and share security docs and pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-02 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 73 min | Recording: Fireflies auto
Attendees: Sahir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aurelia CTO), Rajiv Kapoor (Aurelia Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Aurelia SRE)

[00:00] Sahir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sahir from redwood, and with me is elena who will cover the perf/infra bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:15] Maya: good thanks, a little early for us but all good. appreciate the time.
[00:23] Elena: morning — quick agenda, we want to understand your steady-state, peak bursts, isolation needs for PHI, and then talk about how dedicated reserved capacity maps to that. then next steps around bench and security.
[00:39] Rajiv: yeah that's right. we run inference for several EHR normalization and triage models, roughly 150ms p50 now on our in-house cluster, but the throughput patterns are spiky. we need predictable latency under load.
[00:55] Lena: and from SRE perspective, we need tenant isolation between prod / staging / internal research — can't have cross-tenant noisy neighbor for PHI workloads.
[01:10] Sahir: got it. quick qualification: are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private? where's your preference?
[01:18] Maya: priority is dedicated — security & compliance reasons. hosted api is attractive for dev but prod must be in a dedicated pool or a private vpc.
[01:28] Rajiv: also want to avoid single-tenant hardware per environment for cost reasons; a model where we reserve a pool with logical isolation is preferred.
[01:40] Elena: ok so mixed approach: reserved capacity with node-level isolation (affinity/taints) plus a burst pool that can be shared across customers but with encryption in transit at rest. any hard constraints on region or data residency?
[01:53] Maya: data at rest stays in our VPC, and keys managed by our KMS/HSM. so we need Redwood to support BYOK and bring-your-own-kms integration.
[02:05] Sahir: yes we support KMS integrations and HSM options in the Private/Dedicated offering — we'll share the KMS doc.
[02:12] Rajiv: another thing — can we get strict CPU/GPU isolation so noisy neighbor isn't an issue? We've had contention when other jobs schedule on same host.
[02:22] Elena: on dedicated we can pin workloads to physical GPUs and nodes, plus node isolation (dedicated tenancy) with reserved slots per pool. that prevents co-located tenant jobs. for the burst pool we use work-sharing, but there are controls: concurrency caps, preemption priority, and fallback to smaller quantized models.
[02:44] Maya: fallback to quantized model — interesting, but can that break quality? we need a cutoff threshold.
[02:51] Elena: yes you can configure a quality budget — if primary model out of capacity, route to a quantized variant only if confidence scores above threshold, otherwise queue or fail with graceful degradation.
[03:05] Lena: what's the typical latency hit when moving to 4-bit quantization?
[03:10] Elena: rough ballpark depends on model; for LLM-style decoders, p50 might increase a bit but cost per token drops significantly. we'll include model-specific numbers in the perf matrix.
[03:22] Rajiv: ok can you explain burst sizing? we have 2.5M tokens/day average but 80% of traffic in 4 hours a day.
[03:33] Sahir: common pattern. recommended is base reserved capacity sized for steady-state 95th percentile, plus a burst pool sized to handle X additional concurrent sessions based on your peak qps. do you have concurrency and per-request token estimates?
[03:45] Rajiv: average session ~600 tokens, peak concurrent sessions around 350 today, baseline 80 concurrent.
[03:53] Elena: quick calc: if baseline 80 concurrent mapped to N GPUs for your chosen model, to absorb 350 you'd need about 4-5x capacity during peaks. with reserved + burst we can reserve enough to handle baseline and allow bursts up to commit levels with throttles.
[04:10] Maya: how are costs modeled? are burst hours billed at higher rate?
[04:15] Sahir: pricing model: reserved monthly commit covers base capacity at discounted rate. burst usage beyond commitment billed on-demand; we can also do committed burst blocks for predictable billing if you prefer.
[04:27] Rajiv: what's the minimum commitment? we need to understand financial exposure.
[04:31] Sahir: typical starting point is 3-month commit for a minimum set of GPUs, sliding scale discounts at 6/12 month. i'll send the tier sheet.
[04:39] Lena: we need SLA for latency as well — can you guarantee p95 under X ms?
[04:45] Elena: we can commit to infra-level latency SLOs per model family and sequence length. important note: application-level p95 includes prompt variability and network; we provide token-level latency breakdowns in the Console. for firm guarantees we recommend Dedicated with pinned nodes.
[04:59] Maya: can we pin specific models to nodes? e.g., smaller Llama variant on a different pool?
[05:06] Elena: yes, model pinning and rollout controls are supported. you can create routes so certain calls go to specific pools or model variants, and use canary/AB rollouts.
[05:16] Rajiv: failure modes — if dedicated pool is saturated, what's fallback?
[05:20] Sahir: two options: automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model in another region, or queueing with exponential backoff. we can also define strict rejects if you prefer not to touch hosted resources for PHI.
[05:33] Maya: prefer reject > fallback for PHI unless it's encrypted end-to-end and KMS managed by us.
[05:40] Elena: noted. we'll show config for reject vs fallback and policy toggles.
[05:47] Rajiv: on the network side — VPC peering or private link? we need private connectivity with enforced egress rules.
[05:54] Sahir: Redwood Private offers VPC connectors and private link. for Dedicated we can do customer-managed VPC attachments and strict egress control.
[06:02] Lena: any audit/logging we can export? we need immutable audit logs for inference requests tied back to request ids.
[06:09] Elena: yes, request-level audit logs, model versioning metadata, and trace hooks. logs can be exported to your SIEM and retained per your retention policy.
[06:18] Maya: to move forward, we want a bench run. what do you need from us?
[06:23] Elena: ideally a representative prompts set (10-50 prompts), expected concurrency, max sequence length, and a brief corpus to emulate typical token distribution. Rajiv, you mentioned heatmaps — that will help.
[06:36] Rajiv: i'll export heatmaps and attach. we can provide 30 sample prompts and a synthetic load profile.
[06:42] Sahir: great. we'll do a 2-hour run that includes baseline reserved capacity sim and burst spike test. we'll test both A100 and H100 configs if you want.
[06:54] Maya: yes please include H100, we want to compare perf/cost. also need to test encrypted key performance with BYOK.
[07:02] Elena: BYOK perf test requires a KMS proxy in the loop; small latency added but measurable. we'll include that path.
[07:10] Rajiv: how long to provision a dedicated pool for benchmark?
[07:13] Sahir: for a test lab we can spin ephemeral capacity within 48 hours depending on queue; for Reserved production it's lead time 2-4 weeks for dedicated capacity provisioning.
[07:24] Lena: can we simulate noisy neighbor effects? we want to see worst-case tail latencies.
[07:29] Elena: yes we can run synthetic co-tenancy experiments and show isolation behavior; for dedicated with pinned GPUs you'll see minimal cross-talk.
[07:38] Maya: what's the upgrade rollback story? if a model rollout causes regressions in quality we need auto rollback.
[07:44] Elena: rollouts support canary + thresholds on quality metrics. if regression detected against eval prompts we auto rollback and route to previous model. you can configure detection sensitivity.
[07:56] Rajiv: ok this is useful. question from procurement: what about contract terms on data retention and incident response?
[08:04] Sahir: we'll share the standard enterprise contract and the data processing addendum. we typically allow custom terms for PHI customers; we'll loop in legal if needed.
[08:15] Maya: please include indemnity and breach notification windows.
[08:19] Sahir: noted.
[08:22] [08:22] Lena: small callout — we want to avoid cold starts for large models; does Redwood keep KV cache warm across requests?
[08:30] Elena: yes continuous KV cache and prefix caching are supported; we also have warm pools that keep activations in memory for low-latency paths. that can be part of your reserved footprint.
[08:42] Rajiv: and autoscaling — how quick? we need scale-up under sudden spikes but not let cost explode.
[08:48] Elena: autoscaling has configurable cooldowns, prioritization and rate limits. for burst we use classified priority queues and can spin up extra nodes within minutes depending on hardware availability; faster if you commit reserved burst blocks.
[09:02] Maya: can we set hard caps to prevent runaway cost?
[09:05] Sahir: yes, budget caps and alerts, plus forced rejects. we can also do pre-commit billing so bursts are in a prepaid block to avoid surprises.
[09:14] Rajiv: any partner integrations we should know? monitoring, prometheus exporters etc?
[09:18] Elena: we have prometheus metrics, traces (open-telemetry), and plug-ins for Datadog/Databricks. we'll share samples.
[09:27] Sahir: quick recap and proposed next steps — i'll send pricing + commitment tiers and contract template; elena will produce perf matrix and bench plan; rajiv will send heatmaps and sample prompts; maya will identify compliance contact. then we schedule the 2-hour benchmark week of 12/08. anything else?
[09:47] Maya: sounds good. please also include SOC2 and ISO docs and KMS integration guide.
[09:52] Sahir: will do. last question: timeline to production if bench looks good?
[09:57] Elena: typical ramp: bench + security review 2-3 weeks, procurement + contract 2-4 weeks, provisioning dedicated capacity and initial rollout 2-4 weeks after that. total 6-10 weeks typical.
[10:09] Maya: ok that aligns with our target window. thanks everyone.
[10:15] Sahir: thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and items.
[10:20] [END TRANSCRIPT]
